headings.text: The callback endpoints (mapped to the template)

blocks.html:
pvarki/python-matrix-rmapi is the reference implementation of a product integration API. It integrates Matrix/Synapse into Deploy App, and every part of it maps back to the template and the rmapi callback contract. Read it alongside Scaffold from the template. The runtime architecture of the deployed Matrix stack (Synapse, MAS, LiveKit, Element Call) is documented in Matrix stack (Kubernetes).

What it does

From its README.rst, matrixrmapi has two responsibilities:

  1. Synapse bootstrap — on startup it registers an admin bot, creates the deployment's Space and rooms, and configures their state.
  2. User lifecycle — it receives CRUD callbacks from the core rmapi over mTLS and reflects each event into Synapse.

It is the same shape as a template-generated component integration: a FastAPI app (src/matrixrmapi/app.py) with /api/v1 and /api/v2 routers, an mTLS-guarded usercrud.py, a description.py, a healthcheck.py, and a ui/ bundle.

The app factory and startup

src/matrixrmapi/app.py mirrors the template's get_app() — same CORS-from-manifest regex — but adds a lifespan that launches synapse_startup(app) as a non-blocking background task and initialises app.state.pending_promotions = {}. The HTTP server is up immediately; Synapse bootstrap happens in the background.

The documented startup sequence:

  1. Poll GET /health on Synapse until it responds 200 (up to 5 minutes).
  2. Acquire a file lock and register the admin bot via Synapse's HMAC-signed registration endpoint (idempotent).
  3. Remove rate-limiting for the bot user.
  4. Ensure the Space and four rooms exist.
  5. Apply idempotent state events (name, encryption, join rules, history visibility, topics).
  6. Expose app.state.rooms — the gate the CRUD endpoints check.
  7. Drain any promotions/demotions that arrived before rooms were ready.

The admin bot is created at power level 200 so it can always demote admins (level 100) — a Matrix spec requirement.

The flow the rest of this page describes — background bootstrap, plus a lifecycle callback that can land before Synapse is ready:

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
    participant RM as Core rmapi
    participant API as matrixrmapi
    participant SYN as Synapse

    Note over API,SYN: Startup runs as a non-blocking background task
    API->>SYN: poll GET /health until 200 (up to 5 min)
    API->>SYN: register admin bot, create Space + 4 rooms
    SYN-->>API: ready → app.state.rooms is set

    Note over RM,API: a promotion can arrive before rooms exist
    RM->>API: POST /api/v1/users/promoted (mTLS, CN-pinned)
    alt app.state.rooms not ready yet
        API->>API: queue uid + action in pending_promotions
        API-->>RM: 200 success (deferred)
    else rooms ready
        API->>SYN: set power level 100, force-join admin room
        API-->>RM: 200 success
    end
    Note over API: on startup completion, drain pending_promotions

The callback endpoints (mapped to the template)

src/matrixrmapi/api/usercrud.py implements exactly the template's five stubs, guarded by the same comes_from_rm() CN check against manifest["rasenmaeher"]["certcn"]:

Endpoint Template stub Matrix behaviour
POST /api/v1/users/created user_created Force-joins the user to the Space and three public rooms. If Synapse isn't ready, returns success (auto_join_rooms handles it on first login).
POST /api/v1/users/revoked user_revoked Deactivates and erases the user from Synapse.
POST /api/v1/users/promoted user_promoted Sets power level 100 in Space + public rooms, force-joins the admin channel. Queued if Synapse isn't ready.
POST /api/v1/users/demoted user_demoted Resets power level to 0, kicks from the admin channel. Queued if Synapse isn't ready.
PUT /api/v1/users/updated user_updated No-op — a callsign change requires a new Matrix account.

Deferred queue

Where the template stub would simply return OperationResultResponse(success=True), Matrix shows the real-world subtlety: because Synapse starts slowly, /promoted and /demoted can arrive before app.state.rooms exists. The uid and action are stored in app.state.pending_promotions and drained after startup. If a user is promoted then demoted before Synapse is ready, only the last action survives (the dict key is overwritten). tests/test_crud.py asserts exactly this.

Description and UI

src/matrixrmapi/api/description.py returns a component-type ProductComponent pointing at /ui/matrix/remoteEntry.js — the same convention the template generates — with an icon and a docs URL, and fi/sv/en translations filled in. The ui/ folder is a Vite/Module-Federation React app.

Container startup

  • docker/container-init.sh resolves the magic hostnames into /etc/hosts, runs kw_product_init init /pvarki/kraftwerk-init.json to fetch certificates (skipped if /data/persistent/public/mtlsclient.pem already exists), builds a manifest, fetches a JWT via kc_client_init, and registers Synapse as an OIDC client.
  • docker/entrypoint.sh copies the built UI from /ui_build into /ui_files/matrix, then runs gunicorn "matrixrmapi.app:get_app()" with uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker.

Tests

tests/conftest.py shows how to test the mTLS contract without real certs: a rm_mtlsclient fixture sets the X-ClientCert-DN header to CN=<rasenmaeher certcn>,... (so comes_from_rm() passes), while a plain mtlsclient uses a non-RM CN. tests/test_crud.py asserts that a no-CN call returns 403, that each lifecycle call returns 200 with success=True, and the deferred-queue behaviour above.

Configuration

Key environment variables (from the README): SYNAPSE_URL (default http://synapse:8008), SYNAPSE_REGISTRATION_SECRET (required), SYNAPSE_BOT_USERNAME (default matrixrmapi-bot), SYNAPSE_TOKEN_FILE, and SERVER_DOMAIN (derived from the manifest). Use this as the model for documenting your own integration's config.

Dev workflow for matrixrmapi itself (devel_shell container, uvicorn ... --reload, prek, tox) is covered in its README; the stack-level dev setup is in Set up your dev environment (Docker Compose) / (Kubernetes).
